item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Property and Equipment
text: We evaluate our long-lived assets each quarter for indicators of potential impairment.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Property and Equipment
text: Indicators of impairment include current period losses combined with a history of losses, our decision to relocate or close a store or other location before the end of its previously estimated useful life, or when changes in other circumstances indicate the carrying amount of an asset group may not be recoverable.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Property and Equipment
text: The evaluation for long-lived assets is performed at the lowest level of identifiable cash flows, which is generally the individual store level.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Property and Equipment
text: Long-lived assets with indicators of impairment are evaluated for recoverability by comparing their undiscounted future cash flows with their carrying value.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Property and Equipment
text: If the carrying value is greater than the undiscounted future cash flows, we then measure the asset group's fair value to determine whether an impairment loss should be recognized.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Property and Equipment
text: If the resulting fair value is less than the carrying value, an impairment loss is recognized for the difference between the carrying value and the estimated fair value.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Property and Equipment
text: Impairment losses on property and equipment are recorded as a component of SG&A. Impairment charges for long-lived assets were not material to our consolidated financial statements in fiscal 2023, fiscal 2022, or fiscal 2021.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: We enter into contractual arrangements for the utilization of certain non-owned assets which are evaluated as finance or operating leases upon commencement, and are accounted for accordingly.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Specifically, a contract is or contains a lease when (1) the contract contains an explicitly or implicitly identified asset and (2) we obtain substantially all of the economic benefits from the use of that underlying asset and direct how and for what purpose the asset is used during the term of the contract in exchange for consideration.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: We assess whether an arrangement is or contains a lease at inception of the contract.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Our leases include certain retail locations, warehouse and distribution space, office space, equipment, and vehicles.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: A substantial majority of our leases have remaining lease terms of one to 20 years.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Our real estate leases typically provide the option to extend the lease for five-year terms, and some of our leases include early termination options.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: The lease term used to calculate the right-of-use asset and lease liability at commencement includes the impacts of options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that we will exercise that option.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: When determining whether it is reasonably certain that we will exercise an option at commencement, we consider various existing economic factors, including market conditions, real estate strategies, the nature, length, and terms of the agreement, as well as the uncertainty of the condition of leased equipment at the end of the lease term.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Based on these determinations, we generally conclude that the exercise of renewal options would not be reasonably certain in determining the lease term at commencement.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: The discount rate used to calculate the present value of lease payments is the rate implicit in the lease, when readily determinable.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: As the rate implicit in the lease is rarely readily determinable, we use a secured incremental borrowing rate, which is updated on a quarterly basis, as the discount rate for the present value of lease payments.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Real estate taxes, insurance, maintenance, and operating expenses applicable to the leased asset are generally our obligations under our lease agreements.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: In instances where these payments are fixed, they are included in the measurement of our lease liabilities, and when variable, they are excluded and recognized in the period in which the obligation for those payments is incurred.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Certain of our lease agreements also include rental payments based on an index or rate, and others include rental payments based on a percentage of sales.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: For variable payments dependent upon an index or rate, we apply the active index or rate as of the lease commencement date.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Variable lease payments not based on an index or rate are not included in the measurement of our lease liabilities, as they cannot be reasonably estimated, and are recognized in the period in which the obligation for those payments is incurred.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Leases that have a term of twelve months or less upon commencement are considered short-term in nature.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Short-term leases are not included on the consolidated balance sheets and are expensed on a straight-line basis over the lease term.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: We have also elected to not separate lease and non-lease components for certain classes of assets including real estate and certain equipment.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Leases
text: Our lease agreements do not contain any material residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Business Combinations
text: The assets and liabilities of acquired businesses are recorded at their fair values at the date of acquisition.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Business Combinations
text: The excess of the purchase price over the fair values of the identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed is recorded as goodwill.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Business Combinations
text: During the measurement period, which is up to one year from the acquisition date, we may record adjustments to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed with the corresponding offset to goodwill.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Business Combinations
text: Upon conclusion of the measurement period, any subsequent adjustments are recorded to earnings.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: Goodwill represents the excess of purchase price over the fair value of net assets acquired.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: We do not amortize goodwill, but assess the recoverability of goodwill in the third quarter of each fiscal year, or more often if indicators warrant, by determining whether the fair value of each reporting unit supports its carrying value.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: Each fiscal year, we may assess qualitative factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of each reporting unit is less than its carrying amount as a basis for determining whether it is necessary to complete quantitative impairment assessments, with a quantitative assessment completed periodically or as facts and circumstances warrant.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: During the third quarter of fiscal 2023, we completed our annual assessment of the recoverability of goodwill for our U.S., Canada, and Mexico reporting units, using a quantitative approach.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: The quantitative test for goodwill impairment was performed by determining the fair value of the reporting units using a combination of discounted cash flow and market-based approaches.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: The results of our quantitative analysis indicated that the fair value of each of the reporting units substantially exceeded its respective carrying value, including goodwill.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: There were no impairment charges related to goodwill for fiscal 2023, fiscal 2022, or fiscal 2021.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Goodwill
text: Additional information regarding our goodwill is included in Note 4.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Other Intangible Assets
text: Intangible assets other than goodwill are included in other assets on the consolidated balance sheets.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Other Intangible Assets
text: We amortize the cost of definite-lived intangible assets on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, which range up to approximately 20 years, as this approximates the pattern of expected economic benefit.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Other Intangible Assets
text: We evaluate our definite-lived intangible assets for impairment when evidence exists that certain triggering events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of these assets may not be recoverable.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Other Intangible Assets
text: Intangible assets with indefinite lives are tested in the third quarter of each fiscal year for impairment, or more often if indicators warrant.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Other Intangible Assets
text: During the third quarter of fiscal 2023, we completed our annual assessment of the recoverability of our indefinite-lived intangible assets based on quantitative factors and concluded no impairment losses should be recognized.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Other Intangible Assets
text: There were no impairment losses related to intangible assets for fiscal 2023, fiscal 2022, or fiscal 2021.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Other Intangible Assets
text: Additional information regarding our intangible assets is included in Note 4.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: We have a supplier finance program whereby we have entered into payment processing agreements with several financial institutions.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: Under these agreements, the financial institutions act as our paying agents with respect to accounts payable due to certain suppliers.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: Participating suppliers may, at their sole discretion, elect to receive payment for one or more of our payment obligations, prior to their scheduled due dates, at a discounted price from participating financial institutions.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: We are not a party to the agreements between the participating financial institutions and the suppliers in connection with the program, and our rights and obligations to our suppliers are not impacted.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: We do not reimburse suppliers for any costs they incur for participation in the program.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: We have not pledged any assets as security or provided any guarantees as part of the program.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: We have no economic interest in our suppliers' decisions to participate in the program.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: Our responsibility is limited to making payment to the respective financial institution according to the terms originally negotiated with the supplier, regardless of whether the supplier elects to receive early payment from the financial institution.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: The payment terms we negotiate with our suppliers are consistent, irrespective of whether a supplier participates in the program.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: Our current payment terms with a majority of our suppliers generally range from 30 to 60 days, which we deem to be commercially reasonable.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: Our outstanding payment obligations under our supplier finance program were $514 million at January 28, 2024, and $480 million at January 29, 2023 and are recorded within accounts payable on the consolidated balance sheets.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Supplier Finance Programs
text: The associated payments are included in operating activities within the consolidated statements of cash flows.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Debt
text: We record any premiums or discounts associated with an issuance of long-term debt as a direct addition or deduction to the carrying value of the related senior notes.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Debt
text: We also record debt issuance costs associated with an issuance of long-term debt as a direct deduction to the carrying value of the related senior notes.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Debt
text: Premium, discount, and debt issuance costs are amortized over the term of the respective notes using the effective interest rate method.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: We use derivative instruments in the management of our interest rate exposure on long-term debt and our exposure to foreign currency fluctuations.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: We enter into derivative instruments for risk management purposes only; we do not enter into derivative instruments for trading or speculative purposes.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: All derivative instruments are recognized at their fair values in either assets or liabilities at the balance sheet date and are classified as either current or non-current based on each contract's respective maturity.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: While we enter into master netting arrangements, our policy is to present the fair value of derivative instruments on a gross basis in our consolidated balance sheets.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: Changes in the fair values for derivative instruments designated as cash flow or net investment hedges are recognized in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) until the hedged item is recognized in earnings, which for net investment hedges is upon sale or substantial liquidation of the underlying net investment.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: Changes in fair value of outstanding fair value hedges and the offsetting changes in fair values of the hedged item are recognized in earnings.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: We record realized gains and losses from derivative instruments in the same financial statement line item as the hedged item.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities
text: Cash flows from the settlement of derivative instruments appear in the consolidated statements of cash flows in the same categories as the cash flows of the hedged item.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Self-Insurance Reserves
text: We are self-insured for certain losses related to general liability (including product liability), workers' compensation, employee group medical, and automobile claims.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Self-Insurance Reserves
text: We recognize the expected ultimate cost for claims incurred (undiscounted) at the balance sheet date as a liability.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Self-Insurance Reserves
text: The expected ultimate cost for claims incurred is estimated based upon analysis of historical data and actuarial estimates.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Self-Insurance Reserves
text: We also maintain cybersecurity and privacy liability insurance coverage to help limit our exposure to losses such as those that may be caused by a significant compromise or breach of our data security, as well as property loss coverage.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Self-Insurance Reserves
text: Our self-insurance liabilities, which are included in accrued salaries and related expenses, other accrued expenses, and other long-term liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets, were $1.4 billion at January 28, 2024, and $1.3 billion at January 29, 2023.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Treasury Stock
text: Treasury stock is reflected as a reduction of stockholders' equity at cost.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Treasury Stock
text: We use the weighted average purchase cost to determine the cost of treasury stock that is reissued, if any.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Treasury Stock
text: Excise taxes incurred on share repurchases represent direct costs of the repurchase and are recorded as a part of the cost basis of the shares within treasury stock.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: We recognize revenue, net of expected returns and sales tax, at the time the customer takes possession of merchandise or when a service is performed.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: Our liability for sales returns is estimated based on historical return levels and our expectation of future returns.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: We also recognize a return asset, and corresponding adjustment to cost of sales, for our right to recover the goods returned by the customer, measured at the former carrying amount of the goods, less any expected recovery cost.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: At each financial reporting date, we assess our estimates of expected returns, refund liabilities, and return assets.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: Services revenue is generated through a variety of installation, home maintenance, and professional service programs.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: In these programs, the customer selects and purchases material for a project, and we provide or arrange for professional installation.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: These programs are offered through our stores, online, and in-home sales programs.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: Under certain programs, when we provide or arrange for the installation of a project and the subcontractor provides material as part of the installation, both the material and labor are included in services revenue.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: We recognize services revenue when the service for the customer is complete, which is not materially different from recognizing the revenue over the service period as the substantial majority of our services are completed within one week.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: For products and services sold in stores or online, payment is typically due at the point of sale.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: When we receive payment before the customer has taken possession of the merchandise or the service has been performed, the amount received is recorded as deferred revenue until the sale or service is complete.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: Such performance obligations are part of contracts with expected original durations of typically three months or less.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: As of January 28, 2024 and January 29, 2023, deferred revenue for products and services was $1.7 billion and $2.0 billion, respectively.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: We further record deferred revenue for the sale of gift cards and recognize the associated revenue upon the redemption of those gift cards, which generally occurs within six months of gift card issuance.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: As of both January 28, 2024 and January 29, 2023, our performance obligations for unredeemed gift cards were $1.1 billion.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: Gift card breakage income, which is our estimate of the portion of our outstanding gift card balance not expected to be redeemed, is recognized in net sales and was immaterial in fiscal 2023, fiscal 2022, and fiscal 2021.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: We also have agreements with third-party service providers who directly extend credit to customers, manage our PLCC program, and own the related receivables.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: We have evaluated the third-party entities holding the receivables under the program and concluded that they should not be consolidated.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: The agreement with the primary third-party service provider for our PLCC program expires in 2028, with us having the option, but no obligation, to purchase the existing receivables at the end of the agreement.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Revenue Recognition
text: Deferred interest charges incurred for our deferred financing programs offered to these customers, interchange fees charged to us for their use of the cards, and any profit sharing with the third-party service providers are included in net sales.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Cost of Sales
text: Cost of sales includes the actual cost of merchandise sold and services performed; the cost of transportation of merchandise from vendors to our distribution network, stores, or customers; shipping and handling costs from our stores or distribution network to customers; and the operating cost and depreciation of our sourcing and distribution network.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Cost of Sales
text: Vendor allowances that are not reimbursements of specific, incremental, and identifiable costs are also included within cost of sales.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Vendor Allowances
text: Vendor allowances primarily consist of volume rebates that are earned as a result of attaining certain purchase levels and co-op advertising allowances for the promotion of vendors' products that are typically based on guaranteed minimum amounts with additional amounts being earned for attaining certain purchase levels.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Vendor Allowances
text: These vendor allowances are accrued as earned, with those allowances received as a result of attaining certain purchase levels accrued over the incentive period, which generally concludes at the end of the calendar year, based on estimates of purchases.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Vendor Allowances
text: Volume rebates and certain co-op advertising allowances reduce the carrying cost of inventory and are recognized in cost of sales when the related inventory is sold.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Selling, General and Administrative
text: Selling, general and administrative expenses include compensation and benefits for retail and store support center associates, occupancy and operating costs of retail locations and store support centers, insurance-related expenses, advertising costs, credit and debit card processing fees, and other administrative costs.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Advertising Expense
text: Advertising costs, including digital, television, radio and print, are expensed when the advertisement first appears.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Advertising Expense
text: Certain co-op advertising allowances that are reimbursements of specific, incremental, and identifiable costs incurred to promote vendors' products are recorded as an offset against advertising expense.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Advertising Expense
text: Net advertising expense included in SG&A was $1.1 billion, $1.1 billion, and $1.0 billion for fiscal 2023, 2022, and 2021, respectively.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Stock-Based Compensation
text: We are currently authorized to issue incentive and nonqualified stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units, performance shares, performance units, and deferred shares to certain of our associates and non-employee directors under certain stock incentive plans.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Stock-Based Compensation
text: We measure and recognize compensation expense for all stock-based payment awards made to associates and non-employee directors based on estimated fair values.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Stock-Based Compensation
text: The value of the portion of the award that is ultimately expected to vest is recognized as stock-based compensation expense, on a straight-line basis, over the requisite service period or as restrictions lapse.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Stock-Based Compensation
text: We include estimated forfeitures expected to occur when calculating stock-based compensation expense.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Stock-Based Compensation
text: Additional information on our stock-based payment awards is included in Note 9.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: We provide for federal, state, and foreign income taxes currently payable, as well as for those deferred due to timing differences between reporting income and expenses for financial statement purposes versus tax purposes.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to temporary differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted income tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: The effect of a change in income tax rates is recognized as income or expense in the period that includes the enactment date.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: We routinely evaluate the likelihood of realizing the benefit of our deferred tax assets and may record a valuation allowance if, based on all available evidence, we determine that it is more likely than not that some portion of the tax benefit will not be realized.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: We recognize the effect of income tax positions only if those positions are more likely than not of being sustained.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Recognized income tax positions are measured at the largest amount that is greater than 50% likely of being realized.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Changes in recognition or measurement are reflected in the period in which the change in judgment occurs.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: We recognize interest and penalties related to income tax matters in interest expense and SG&A, respectively, on our consolidated statements of earnings.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Accrued interest and penalties related to income tax matters are recognized in other accrued expenses and other long-term liabilities on our consolidated balance sheets.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: We file a consolidated U.S. federal income tax return which includes certain eligible subsidiaries.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Non-U.S. subsidiaries and certain U.S. subsidiaries, which are consolidated for financial reporting purposes, are not eligible to be included in our consolidated U.S. federal income tax return.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: Separate provisions for income taxes have been determined for these entities.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: For unremitted earnings of our non-U.S. subsidiaries, we are required to make an assertion regarding reinvestment or repatriation for tax purposes.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: For any earnings that we do not make a permanent reinvestment assertion, we recognize a provision for deferred income taxes.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: For earnings where we have made a permanent reinvestment assertion, no provision is recognized.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: See Note 6 for further discussion.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: We are subject to global intangible low-taxed income tax, an incremental tax on foreign income.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Income Taxes
text: We have made an accounting election to record this tax in the period the tax arises.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Comprehensive Income
text: Comprehensive income includes net earnings adjusted for certain gains and losses that are excluded from net earnings and recognized within accumulated other comprehensive loss as a component of equity, which consist primarily of foreign currency translation adjustments.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Comprehensive Income
text: Accumulated other comprehensive loss also includes net losses on cash flow hedges that were immaterial as of January 28, 2024 and January 29, 2023.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Comprehensive Income
text: Reclassifications from accumulated other comprehensive loss into earnings were immaterial in fiscal 2023, fiscal 2022, and fiscal 2021.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Foreign Currency Translation
text: Assets and liabilities denominated in a foreign currency are translated into U.S. dollars at the current rate of exchange on the last day of the reporting period.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Foreign Currency Translation
text: Revenues and expenses are translated using average exchange rates for the period, and equity transactions are translated using the actual rate on the day of the transaction.

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Foreign Currency Translation
text: Cumulative foreign currency translation adjustments recorded in accumulated other comprehensive loss as of January 28, 2024 and January 29, 2023 were losses of $365 million and $597 million, respectively.

SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements

item_title: SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES > Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements
text: The guidance does not affect the recognition, measurement, or financial statement presentation of obligations covered by supplier finance programs.

Redemption.
All of our senior notes may be redeemed by us at any time, in whole or in part, at the redemption price plus accrued interest up to the redemption date.

With respect to the 5.875% 2036 notes and the 5.125% 2025 notes, the redemption price is equal to the greater of (1) 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, or (2) the sum of the present values of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest on the notes to be redeemed that would be due after the related redemption date.

With respect to all other notes, prior to the Par Call Date, as defined in the respective notes, the redemption price is equal to the greater of (1) 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed or (2) the sum of the present values of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to the Par Call Date.
On or after the Par Call Date, the redemption price is equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes.

Additionally, if a Change in Control Triggering Event occurs, as defined in the notes, holders of all such notes have the right to require us to redeem those notes at 101% of the aggregate principal amount of the notes plus accrued interest up to the redemption date.

The fair value of an asset is considered to be the price at which the asset could be sold in an orderly transaction between unrelated knowledgeable and willing parties.
A liability's fair value is defined as the amount that would be paid to transfer the liability to a new obligor, rather than the amount that would be paid to settle the liability with the creditor.
Assets and liabilities recorded at fair value are measured using a three-tier fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value.
The levels of the fair value hierarchy are:
• Level 1: observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities;
• Level 2: inputs other than quoted prices in active markets in Level 1 that are either directly or indirectly observable; and
• Level 3: unobservable inputs for which little or no market data exists, therefore requiring management judgment to develop the Company's own models with estimates and assumptions.

Restrictions on the restricted stock issued under the Plans generally lapse over various periods up to five years.
At the grant date of the award, recipients of restricted stock are granted voting rights and generally receive dividends on unvested shares, paid in the form of cash on each dividend payment date.
Dividends paid on unvested shares were immaterial for fiscal 2023, fiscal 2022, and fiscal 2021.
Additionally, the majority of our restricted stock awards may become non-forfeitable upon the associate's attainment of age 60, provided the associate has had five years of continuous service.
We have also granted performance share awards under the Plans.

These awards provide for the issuance of shares of our common stock at the end of the three-year performance cycle based upon our performance against target average ROIC and operating profit over that performance cycle.

Additionally, the awards become non-forfeitable upon the associate's attainment of age 60, provided the associate has had five years of continuous service and minimum performance targets are achieved.
Recipients of performance share awards have no voting rights until the shares are issued following completion of the performance period.
Dividend equivalents accrue on the performance shares (as reinvested shares) and are paid upon the payout of the award based upon the actual number of shares earned.
The fair value of the restricted stock and performance shares is based on the closing stock price on the date of grant and is expensed over the period during which the restrictions lapse.
Restricted Stock Units.
Each restricted stock unit entitles the associate to one share of common stock to be received upon vesting up to five years after the grant date.
Additionally, the majority of these awards may become non-forfeitable upon the associate reaching age 60, provided the associate has had five years of continuous service.
Recipients of restricted stock units have no voting rights until the vesting of the award.
Recipients receive dividend equivalents that accrue on unvested units and are paid out in the form of additional shares of stock on the vesting date.
The fair value of the restricted stock units is based on the closing stock price on the date of grant and is expensed over the period during which the units vest.
